title: October 25 — Hilbert–Pólya through Rajapinta prime-delay loops (June 2026 archaeology)
summary: A June 2026 draft reframes Hilbert–Pólya as a reciprocal delay-coupled phase-network and states an unproved Prime Orbit Condition (closed-loop transit time log p, requisite weights and cancellation of non-prime loops). A small Python script evaluates a regularized truncated prime explicit-formula sum; its README reports first-20-zero RMS 0.114→0.0052 as the prime cutoff grows from 3 to 500. That is a known arithmetic reconstruction, not an independently realized self-adjoint delay-network spectrum. The paper's separate 700-site test/code is not included in this repository, and its formal self-adjointness and determinant-identification claims were not independently checked. Connect the prime-log DSP artifact and older failed generic prime-trace test only as conceptual comparisons; no direct lineage is documented.

nodes.claim: Drafts a Rajapinta–Takens Hilbert–Pólya candidate: linearize a phase network with structural time delays, treat prime logarithms as primitive closed-loop transit times, and ask whether the resulting delay operator can have both the exact prime-orbit trace weights and a self-adjoint realization.
nodes.survived: The Prime Orbit Condition (POC) is an explicit target rather than a vague resemblance between chaos and Riemann zeros. Included truncated_poc_engine.py evaluates a Gaussian-damped prime-loop explicit-formula approximation without supplying zero locations to N_X; the repository reports RMS error to the first 20 known zero ordinates falling from 0.114 at X=3 to ~0.0052 at X=500. The paper explicitly identifies simultaneous POC-realizability and self-adjointness as the unproved core; finite cutoffs are useful demonstrations of the prime-explicit-formula dictionary.
nodes.killed: No RH proof or constructed self-adjoint operator with exactly the zeta-zero spectrum. The finite numerical curve comes from the established explicit-formula machinery and a cutoff-dependent smoothing window, not an independently generated network operator; known zeros are present in the script for scoring and figure annotations. The paper cites a separate 700-site engine not present in this repository. Its claimed general self-adjointness of a retarded-delay history generator, matching of entire determinants, and de Bruijn–Newman physical identification need independent mathematical scrutiny, and the infinite-limit/realizability gap is open.

edges.why: The earlier audio tool implements log-prime-modulated delay arms as sound design; the later paper interprets log p as primitive closed-walk transit time in a candidate spectrum. This is a shared mathematical motif, not a code inheritance, an operator construction or evidence for RH.

BirthOfClockfield's audit showed generic GOE-like spectral repulsion and a null prime-log trace; this later paper demands exact loop times/weights rather than equating chaos statistics with arithmetic zeros. A methodological contrast, not a demonstrated direct historical derivation.

motifs.title: Prime-log interference is not the missing Hilbert–Pólya operator
motifs.description: PrimeCrystalVST makes incommensurate log-prime arm interference audible; BirthOfClockfield shows generic random-matrix level statistics have no prime-specific trace; HilbertPolyaReintepretation states the much stronger exact prime-orbit weights and cancellation problem. Finite explicit-formula reconstruction is numerically useful but does not solve the self-adjoint operator existence problem.
